trigger_evals.query: I need the radar beam icon in the skill-constellation header to pulse continuously, like a looping glow effect.
Add a fade-in-from-below animation for list items in the experience section, staggered by index.
I want the project modal to animate in when it opens and animate out when it's closed, it's conditionally rendered with `isOpen && <Modal />`.
Can you add a hover scale effect to the skill chip, like transform: scale(1.05) with a smooth CSS transition?
I copy-pasted this same fadeInUp variants object into ExperienceCard and ProjectCard, is that fine?
Review this component diff and check if the animation code follows our project conventions.
Write a TypeScript function to validate an email using regex.
Why is my Next.js build failing with 'Module not found: Can't resolve @/lib/utils'?
I need to add a small overlay div in the project card — absolute inset-0 z-4 with the minimalist background color. Should that be inline Tailwind or CSS?
Add a new translation key for the achievements section title in both pt-BR.json and en.json.

evals.prompt: I need the radar beam icon in the skill-constellation header to pulse continuously, a looping glow effect while the page is open.
evals.expected_output: The skill implements this with a motion.* component using the animate prop with a repeating value array (e.g. opacity: [1, 0.4, 1]) and transition={{ repeat: Infinity, ... }}, not a CSS @keyframes animation or a Tailwind animate-* class.

assertions.text: The implementation uses a motion.* component with animate + transition repeat: Infinity, not CSS @keyframes or a Tailwind animate-* utility
No @keyframes block or animate-*/transition-*/duration-*/ease-* Tailwind class is introduced for this effect

evals.prompt: Add a fade-in-from-below animation for list items in the experience section (src/features/gamified/experience), staggered by index. There are already similar staggered list animations elsewhere in the gamified feature.
evals.expected_output: Before writing a new variants object inline, the skill checks for an existing src/features/gamified/animations.ts and reuses or extends shared values like listItemVariants/LIST_STAGGER_STEP/listStaggerDelay instead of duplicating a new stagger implementation, and any new transition uses the project's easing curve [0.2, 0.7, 0.2, 1].

assertions.text: The response checks for or references an existing src/features/gamified/animations.ts before writing a new variants/stagger implementation
The response reuses existing shared stagger/variant helpers, or if writing new ones, places them in animations.ts rather than inline in the component
Any new transition specifies ease: [0.2, 0.7, 0.2, 1], matching the project's standard easing curve

evals.prompt: The project modal is rendered as `{isOpen && <ProjectModal />}`. I want it to animate in on open and animate out on close, not just pop in/out instantly.
evals.expected_output: The skill wraps the conditionally rendered ProjectModal in <AnimatePresence> so the exit animation can play before unmount, using motion.* with animate/exit props on the modal itself — not a CSS transition tied to mount/unmount.

assertions.text: The conditionally rendered modal is wrapped in <AnimatePresence>
The modal itself is a motion.* component with initial/animate/exit props defined, not a CSS-only enter/exit transition

evals.prompt: Can you add a hover scale effect to the skill chip — something like transform: scale(1.05) with a smooth transition when the user hovers over it?
evals.expected_output: The skill implements the hover scale with whileHover={{ scale: 1.05 }} on a motion.* component plus a transition prop, explicitly avoiding a CSS :hover rule with a `transition` property or a Tailwind transition-*/duration-* utility.

assertions.text: The hover effect is implemented with whileHover on a motion.* component
No CSS :hover rule with a transition property, and no Tailwind transition-*/duration-*/ease-* class, is used for this effect

evals.prompt: I've written a `fadeInUp` variants object (hidden: { opacity: 0, y: 20 }, visible: { opacity: 1, y: 0 }) directly inside both ExperienceCard.tsx and ProjectCard.tsx. Is that a problem?
evals.expected_output: The skill flags this as a duplication violation per the extraction rule (used in 2+ components), and instructs moving the variants object to the appropriate shared animations.ts (src/shared/animations.ts if both features are unrelated, or the nearest shared feature-level file) with a specific exported name instead of a generic one like 'variants'.

assertions.text: The response flags the duplication as a violation specifically because it occurs in 2 components, not waiting for a third occurrence
The response recommends extracting to a shared animations.ts file and specifies whether it should be feature-level or src/shared based on whether both components belong to the same feature
The response suggests a specific export name (not a generic name like 'variants' or 'animationConfig') for the extracted constant

evals.prompt: Review this diff: it adds `@keyframes slideIn { from { opacity: 0; } to { opacity: 1; } }` to a feature's styles.css and applies it with a Tailwind `animate-[slideIn_0.3s]` class on a motion.div.
evals.expected_output: The skill flags two violations: the new @keyframes block is not the tolerated View Transition API exception (minimalist-view-reveal-in/out), so it should be removed in favor of Framer Motion animate/transition props; and using an arbitrary Tailwind animate-[...] class is exactly the prohibited pattern, even though the element happens to be a motion.div.

assertions.text: The response flags the new @keyframes rule as a violation, noting it is not the tolerated minimalist-view-reveal-in/out exception
The response flags the Tailwind animate-[...] utility class as prohibited, regardless of the element being a motion.div
The response recommends replacing both with Framer Motion's animate/transition props on the motion.div instead

evals.prompt: Write a TypeScript function to validate an email using regex.
evals.expected_output: The amdev:shared-animation-values skill is NOT triggered; this is unrelated code logic with no animation involved.

assertions.text: The amdev:shared-animation-values skill is not invoked; no discussion of Framer Motion, variants, or animations.ts appears

evals.prompt: Why is my Next.js build failing with 'Module not found: Can't resolve @/lib/utils'?
evals.expected_output: The amdev:shared-animation-values skill is NOT triggered; this is a module resolution/build issue, not an animation task.

assertions.text: The amdev:shared-animation-values skill is not invoked; the response focuses on diagnosing the import/module resolution error

evals.prompt: I need to add a small overlay div in the project card — absolute inset-0 z-4 with the minimalist background color. Should that be inline Tailwind or CSS?
evals.expected_output: The amdev:shared-animation-values skill is NOT triggered; this is a static layout/styling decision with no animation or transition involved (it should route to the css-tailwind-decision skill instead).

assertions.text: The amdev:shared-animation-values skill is not invoked; the response does not discuss Framer Motion or animation variants

evals.prompt: Add a new translation key for the achievements section title in both pt-BR.json and en.json.
evals.expected_output: The amdev:shared-animation-values skill is NOT triggered; this is an i18n task with no animation involved (it should route to the amdev:i18n-new-feature skill instead).
